_wo1082TownTypeOrderNote: WO-1082 SECTION 4a (OWNER RULING 2026-08-26): Lumberyard, Foundry and Silo are the LAST THREE tiles of the Town build palette - they are the only rows carved out of the free 15-second first-build grace (BuildModeController isPallet) and the only rows that take ~7.68 minutes. THE LEVER IS THIS ARRAY'S ORDER, and that is not obvious: BuildPaletteVM.AggregateOfType concatenates CatalogRegistry.OfType(type) TYPE-MAJOR, one whole type after another, so EVERY Collector row trails EVERY Resource row no matter where it sits in structures-catalog entries[]. The three containers are Resource; collector_farm and collector_forge are Collector - so while Resource led this array, moving rows inside the catalog could never put the containers last, and WO-1082 section 2 (which assumed one flat array order) was wrong about that. Collector now leads, so the flat WO-963 strip reads: Lumber Mill, Crafting Station, Weaponsmith (the three authored displayOrder rows) -> Farm, Iron Mine, Crystal Mine, Echo Hollow, Store, Armorer, Cathedral of Magic, Barracks -> Lumberyard, Foundry, Silo. THIS IS AN ORDER CHANGE ONLY: same two types, same membership, same lockedIds, same paletteGroups, no cost, no build time, no displayOrder touched, and the tutorial still opens on collector_lumbermill (displayOrder 10). Every other consumer reads catalogTypes as a SET (BuildCategoryRegistry.Types, BuildPaletteGroupsRegression, TutorialStepReachabilityRegression), so nothing else can see this order. It also agrees with _storageIsLastRuling: Storage is last in the grouped view AND in the flat All view.
_storageIsLastRuling: OWNER RULING 2026-08-25, felt-testing build 2026.08.25.341262: Storage is the LAST palette group in the Town row. Verbatim: 'Storage should be last, as those take a real building and 7 min' and 'so if you start two you have to wait or ad to continue'. THE REASON IS THE RULING: a store consumes a real building footprint AND a builder-queue slot for ~7 minutes, and the queue has only 2 free slots, so starting two stores stalls the player into waiting or watching an ad. Offering them FIRST sells the most expensive, least felt purchase before the producers that make the town work. ORDER IS Producers, Trade, Civic, Storage. Pinned by BuildPaletteGroupsRegression - moving Storage off the end turns that suite RED, deliberately.
_paletteGroupsNote: WO-1167 (owner ask 2026-08-24: 'is that done grouping by collector producer storage defense? For build menu and UI'). 'paletteGroups' is an OPTIONAL, ORDERED, DISPLAY-ONLY block on a verb row: each group names a label + the catalog ROLE strings (structures-catalog 'role', the WO-1161 open vocabulary) whose cards render under that header, in authored group order. RULES, enforced by BuildPaletteGroupsRegression: (1) a card whose role names NO group falls into a trailing 'Other' bucket - NEVER dropped, so a brand-new building with a brand-new role appears with ZERO code change (the owner's standing rule); (2) a group with no renderable members renders NOTHING - no empty header; (3) order WITHIN a group is the existing WO-963 displayOrder sort - grouping adds headers, it does not re-sort; (4) buildType/catalogTypes/lockedIds are untouched - nothing re-maps, no id changes (ids are frozen save keys). The grouping axis is ROLE, deliberately NOT 'type': Farm and Lumber Mill are Collector while Silo/Lumberyard/Foundry are Resource, so 'type' splits producers from their stores down the middle - exactly the wrong picture. ⛔ NO ROLE LIST MAY EXIST IN C# - the groups live HERE and only here (WO-1161: a role list in code is one fact written twice).
notes: Build-verb -> catalog-type mapping (owner 2026-07-10 generic build-mode; WO-673 taxonomy 2026-07-11). ONE generic entry BuildModeController.EnterBuildMode(BuildType) is parameterised by 'buildType'; each row maps it to the CatalogType(s) that feed its palette + the unlock-gated ids to filter. Loaded at startup by BuildCategoryRegistry (Village) via CanonicalJson (Resources-first, WebGL-safe). Keep the Resources + StreamingAssets copies byte-equal. 'buildType' / 'catalogTypes' are enum NAMES (StringEnumConverter). 'lockedIds' are catalog ids kept in the catalog but filtered out of THIS verb's palette until their unlock ships. WO-673 (owner ruling 2026-07-11, displays Town / Defenses / Walls): Town = the player-placed functional buildings (Resource + Collector, always on -- WO-682 removed ff.strategicplacement 2026-07-13; supersedes the 2026-06-27 'Defensive only' palette ruling); Defense keeps towers/gates; Walls split out (claimed-outpost wall canon). The jeweler unlock-gate moved from Defense to Town (it is a Resource row). Collector/Support remain as standalone legacy verbs. WO-1010 D21 (owner D8 resolution 2026-08-09): the Walls row's 'label' is the DISPLAY string for the build screen's right-edge quick-tab -- renamed 'Castle Structures' (walls + gates-to-come, verticality later). DISPLAY ONLY: buildType keys + catalogTypes unchanged, nothing re-maps. WO-948 (owner ruling 2026-08-10): walls BUILD at level 1 ONLY (CoC model) -- 'wall_stone' is locked out of the Walls palette here; the catalog ROW survives so existing saves replay/sell placed stone walls (BaseLayoutLoader resolves via CatalogRegistry and never consults these lockedIds). Stone is reached by UPGRADING a placed wood wall (wall_wood maxLevel 2); steel/spiked stay WO-904's behind raid-steal. WO-1013 (2026-08-10): 'visibleLockedIds' is a DIFFERENT axis from 'lockedIds' -- id -> lock-reason WORDS, rendered as a visible card (normal cost shown) that cannot be armed until the id's persisted unlock flag flips (ProgressionUnlocks / SeenTutorials 'unlock.<id>'). The Arcane Spire card is visible-locked 'Recover the plans' from minute one; the wave-2 Castle Defense Plans drop lifts it.
